To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
probabilistic noninterference is a sound notion of information flow security for protocols and that it can be used for a quantitative security analysis of probabilistics protocols.
probabilistic protocols can be analyzed by a combination of probabilistic process algebra, process similarity and quantitative measures of fairness.

(1) we advocate the use of probabilistic process algebra to formally specify probabilistic protocols and to reason about their correctness; (2) we introduce a quantitative analysis technique for the security of probabilistic protocols, based on approximate noninterference and probabilistic bisimulation; (3) we apply the proposed technique to the quantitative analysis of a probabilistically non-deterministic nonrepudiable protocol; (4) the quantitative analysis shows that the protocol has a fairness degree of 0.8
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: - how to formally model the probabilistic behaviour of cryptographic protocols; - what are the appropriate notions of security and correctness for probabilistic protocols; and - how to analyse probabilistic protocols in a quantitative way, i.e. to estimate the degree of fairness or the probability of a protocol to reach its goal.
